title: Voltage: open L2
points: MPC makes a forecast-based plan. SAC is a saved learned controller.
Check limits first. Then compare penalty score J; smaller is preferred after the checks pass.
note: The feeder is a synthetic SMART-DS Greensboro-area example, not a measured utility circuit. The command sets active- and reactive-power participation for an inverter fleet. MPC, model predictive control, uses a system model and a short forecast to calculate a plan under limits; here the proposed command is the first step of that plan. SAC, Soft Actor–Critic, is a saved controller learned from rewards. It produces a proposal from old weights without training again. The default calculation covers medium-voltage (MV) phases and MV line currents, with simplified low-voltage (LV) aggregation. Feasible means the proposal passes the limits represented by that model. Compare the penalty score J only after checking those limits; smaller J is preferred for this stated objective. Run L0 and L1 first.
caption: Synthetic SMART-DS teaching feeder; not an operating utility circuit.

title: MPC plans; SAC proposes
points: Both tools propose control settings. The same numerical check tests their voltage and current limits.
note: MPC uses a model and a short forecast to optimize a plan; this lab applies its first action. SAC is a saved policy learned through reinforcement learning; it produces a new control proposal using old weights, without training again. Neither is the coordinating LLM. The outer agent can choose which permitted study to request. L2 calls both tools directly and displays their checks; this cell alone is not a live LLM agent. Later recorded P3 figures illustrate Llama coordinating the existing tools. Define per unit when the control-limit slide introduces the voltage scale: 1.0 p.u. is the stated base value. Explain MILP and WLS only in their respective cases.
caption: MPC: model predictive control. SAC: Soft Actor–Critic. These are control tools inside the larger workflow.

title: Control settings and limits
points: a sets active-power participation; b sets reactive-power participation.
Check the inverter limits, modeled voltages and allowed line current.
note: Active power delivers net energy; reactive power supports the AC voltage and current balance. The command uses P_i = a S_i and Q_i = b S_i. Its bounds are 0 <= a <= 1, |b| <= 0.44 and a^2 + b^2 <= 1. Modeled voltages must be between 0.95 and 1.05 per unit (p.u.), where values are divided by a stated base. RATING_FRACTION=0.80 sets allowed current to 80% of the nominal rating. The displayed current percentage uses this reduced allowance as its denominator. Passing the inverter bounds alone does not show that network limits pass.
caption: Active and reactive settings share the inverter’s power limit.

title: A tool is a Python function in this lab
points: A tool takes defined inputs and returns evidence. The notebook lets you see both.
note: Find the actual function call on the next slide. The first two cell lines set the load scale and current allowance; the helper returns numerical proposals, checks and a table for plotting. A tool can be an optimizer, simulator, estimator, lookup or evidence checker. It is not the LLM itself. The student initiates this direct function call with the play button. In the separate recorded workflow Llama selects a named action, the Python application validates that action and its inputs, then invokes a permitted numerical function. Do not claim that the L2 helper uses a live agent gateway. Saving a notebook is separate from keeping a runtime: after a reset, rerun setup and earlier cells.
caption: L2 calls lab.voltage_lab(LOAD_SCALE, RATING_FRACTION) directly. Recorded agent coordination is separate.

title: Run L2 with the default inputs
points: Run all of L2 to calculate the MPC plan and check the saved SAC controller’s proposal.
Read feasible, current_step_J and max_allowed_current_pct.
note: Start with LOAD_SCALE=1.0 and RATING_FRACTION=0.80. The saved SAC actor produces a new proposal by inference; it is not trained in this cell. Both proposals pass the default classroom checks. MPC has the lower current-step J for this case and objective. This single result does not establish a universal control advantage. The output field feasible reports whether the modeled limits pass; current_step_J is this step’s penalty score, and max_allowed_current_pct is maximum current as a percentage of the reduced allowance.

title: Read the voltage and current plots
points: Left: compare the sorted modeled voltages with the allowed band.
Right: compare line current with the 100% allowed-current limit.
note: The left panel sorts each voltage curve separately. The same horizontal position means the same rank, not necessarily the same physical bus. The right panel reports current relative to the reduced allowance. Use the output table for exact extrema and feasibility; do not decide acceptance from a plot alone.
caption: Reference L2 plots; rerun L2 to calculate plots for your inputs.

title: Check limits before comparing scores
points: Default MPC passes: current use 73.62%, penalty score J about 0.03110.
Default saved SAC passes: current use 51.68%, J about 0.43643.
note: In the reference execution, MPC returns a=0.960307 and b=-0.111114, with Vmin=1.023874 and Vmax=1.038709 p.u. SAC returns a=0.340066 and b=0.014024, with Vmin=1.013243 and Vmax=1.030000 p.u. Values may vary slightly with the solver or dependency version. Lower current use need not mean lower J, because the objective also includes service and control terms. Check feasibility before comparing J. Both voltage extrema are within the stated 0.95–1.05 p.u. band for this represented MV model.
caption: Reference L2 output with LOAD_SCALE=1.0 and RATING_FRACTION=0.80.

title: A rule and a tool result answer different questions
points: A document can tell us the limit. A numerical tool tells us how the proposal compares with it.
Keep the source, the measured or calculated value, and the remaining checks together.
note: Stanford connection: the lecture’s WikiChat discussion, pp.17–25, separates finding material from checking factual claims. Apply the habit to a grid study: retrieving a current limit is different from calculating current for a candidate. The displayed 99.604410% value belongs to the separate archived P3 OpenDSS replay, not to the learner’s fresh L2 result. This example supports only that current check under its recorded model. A sentence, retrieved document or citation does not establish full-network feasibility. Treat the input limits as the task policy. A text source describes the rule; the solver evaluates the particular proposal.
caption: Teaching analogy. The number shown comes from the recorded P3 replay, which is separate from L2.
source_label: Monica Lam. CS224V Agentic AI, Lecture 1: Introduction. Stanford University, Fall 2026, pp.17–25; recorded P3 current check.

title: Exercise 1: tighten the current allowance
points: In L2, change only RATING_FRACTION from 0.80 to 0.75. Predict, then rerun.
For each method, report feasible, allowed-current use and current_step_J.
Does a PASS cover the full medium- and low-voltage network? Explain.
note: Allow one minute to predict, two minutes to edit and run, and one minute to report. Keep LOAD_SCALE=1.0. Reference allowed-current use is 78.527895% for MPC and 54.854158% for SAC; both remain feasible. Do not ask learners to find a rejection that this edit does not produce. The default model still covers MV only.

title: Change one number and explain the difference
points: A tighter allowance makes the same current a larger percentage of that allowance.
At 0.75, MPC uses 78.53% and SAC 54.85%. Both pass this particular test.
note: Use this visual immediately after the first exercise debrief. It shows the measured reference MPC outputs, rounded to two decimal places, for RATING_FRACTION 0.80 and 0.75. The SAC result is also computed in the notebook but is not drawn here. Both proposals pass this particular tighter test. The result is not a general guarantee for other loads or limits. Ask pairs to explain the denominator in the percentage. Restore the default before moving to L3’s independent archived case. This combines the original numerical debrief with the visual explanation. Compare both methods before restoring RATING_FRACTION=0.80.
caption: Reference L2 exercise: MPC uses 73.62% of the default allowance and 78.53% after the change.
source_label: Classroom Labs L2, cell classroom-007; verified default and exercise outputs.

title: Reset L2 before reading old model choices
points: Restore the default values and rerun L2.
L3–L5 use the original test_01 case, separate from your changed L2 experiment.
note: Make the experiment boundary explicit. L3 loads a separate preserved context into pool. It does not inherit the fresh L2 case or the participant's edits. Do not pair an edited L2 result with the test_01 model explanation as though the model had seen those new inputs.

title: What runs now and what was recorded
points: The current cell calculates new results. The saved Llama reply keeps its original inputs.
Changing your lab input does not rewrite the recorded agent study.
note: Point to these evidence modes throughout the session. Default classroom cells calculate fresh results without a live language-model call. L10B displays verified historical Llama choices, original reasons and associated recorded results. Changing your L2 or L6 input does not change those old replies. The final control-room diagrams are a proposed teaching design, not evidence of a deployed utility platform. No new equipment operation occurs in any of these modes. FRESH means calculated during the current execution. SAVED POLICY means old weights used for new inference. ARCHIVED ACTUAL LLM means an old reply with its original inputs and timing. This slide comes just before L3 so the distinction is applied immediately.
caption: Three explicitly labeled teaching modes used throughout this workshop.

title: L3 opens a separate recorded case
points: Run L3. Read the original case ID, requested operations and recorded seconds.
These reasons are old model replies. Displaying them makes no new model call.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L3; cell classroom-010; archived test_01 context.
note: The output contains three actual replies from the frozen response-selection study. Ask learners to identify the operation and numerical parameters requested by each reply. The reported seconds measure the original model calls, not today's display cell. Keep this archived context separate from the fresh L2 comparison.

title: What did the models choose?
points: Different wording can request the same tool and numbers.
The notebook groups matching trials. An explanation alone does not show that limits pass.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L3; cell classroom-010; archived test_01 context.
note: The three old replies reduce to two distinct operations after matching their tool names and numerical parameters. The vote keeps one contribution per model. In test_01, two models vote for the Q-relaxation trial, which relaxes a reactive-power restriction in that declared test. This diagram shows the old input and choices; it is not a new vote after a learner edits L2. Grouping matching trials avoids counting different wording as different physical proposals.
caption: Three old replies request two distinct operations; two votes select reactive-power relaxation.

title: Run L4: check the old choice again
points: After L3, run L4. Python checks the selected proposal again for its original case.
Compare majority vote with the saved LinUCB selector on that same case.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L4; cell classroom-013; fresh checks of archived choices.
note: The selector is frozen and makes no training updates in this lesson. L4 applies the archived selected operation to its original test context and runs a fresh numerical check. This is a replay with new verification, not a new language-model decision or an online learning experiment. LinUCB is a learned selector that scores the available choices from context; its saved settings stay fixed here.

title: Separate the old choice from the new check
points: Both selectors choose the same reactive-power relaxation trial and pass the new MV check.
Predicted reward is a learned score. Read new_check_passes for the engineering check.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L4; cell classroom-013; fresh checks of archived choices.
note: The reference J is about 0.031082 for both selectors. The predicted reward is around -0.0075. It is a learned score, not a feasibility flag. Read new_check_passes for the engineering result. This one case does not show that learned selection is better than voting.
caption: Reference L4 output: old selector choices, new numerical checks of the original case.

title: Run L5: check what the model covers
points: Keep RUN_OPENDSS=False. Run L5 and read the table and optional_mode message.
L5 checks the original test_01 MV-MPC plan. OpenDSS is disabled.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L5; cell classroom-016; MV-only default model.
note: L5 rebuilds the original test_01 case and runs a new check on its original MV-MPC incumbent, meaning the baseline plan saved with that case. This is not the reactive-power-relaxation candidate checked in L4. With RUN_OPENDSS=False, L5 checks only the reduced model and reports that OpenDSS is disabled. This CPU route performs no new full-feeder AC check. A wider-model study saved earlier is not a result calculated today. Model scope means the network parts and physical effects that a check represents.

title: A PASS covers only the model checked
points: This check covers medium-voltage (MV) phases and currents, not all low-voltage (LV) equipment.
For a full MV/LV request, get the wider check or HOLD.

title: Voltage checkpoint: say what ran
points: L2 makes new proposals; L3 shows old replies; L4–L5 run new checks on test_01.
Report the inputs, proposal, model coverage and result before naming the next step.

note: Give pairs 30 seconds to describe the sequence without calling every step an AI decision. L2 calculates an MPC plan and a saved-policy proposal for the current classroom inputs. L3 displays old model replies. L4 runs new checks of the selected trials; L5 checks the original archived plan and its model coverage. Numerical tools provide the physical evidence.
